lines.text: The courtroom is silent when the sealed file is read aloud. A man who died in prison in 2009 is declared innocent, twenty-eight years late. His daughter weeps. The city finally knows what was buried.

Elias Vane is not charged. He broke no law — he only ever pointed. He resigns from the archive, and on his last day he leaves one thing on the detective's desk: a small black envelope, sealed with a silver anchor. Inside, a single line: 'There are more files. You know where to look.'
Season One is closed. The Anchorman is known. But the archive is deep, the shelves are long — and somewhere in the dark, the next envelope is already waiting.
The Cold Case Unit was founded by one man: Captain Harlan Voss. Tonight he is dead in his own archive room — and the file he was carrying is gone.
Six cases. Six black envelopes. One silver anchor. The Unit has been following a stranger's breadcrumbs for a year, and tonight the trail ends here, in the dark between the shelves.
You are the detective the Unit sends when the case is its own. Solve the murder. Then find the man who has been sending the envelopes — and ask him why.

solve.solutionHTML:
Corinne Hale killed Captain Harlan Voss on the night he was going to deliver the sealed file from the 1998 Harbor Lights trial — the file proving she, as defence attorney, had buried a witness statement that would have freed an innocent man. Voss called her at 21:05 to tell her he was giving the Unit the file that night. She met him in the archive at 21:30 — her own calendar says so — brought him coffee, and dissolved six tablets of his own heart medication in his thermos. She collected the refill herself three days earlier, signing for it in her own name. Her fingerprint, lifted from the underside of the thermos lid where her wipe missed, is the last link.

And the Anchorman is Elias Vane, the Unit's own archivist — Voss's partner from 1998, the young detective who found the buried witness statement and watched it vanish. He could not prove who buried it, so for twenty-eight years he nudged the Cold Case Unit to reopen the cases the burial had touched — one black envelope, one silver anchor seal, one line pointing at the buried thread. Six envelopes this season; twenty-two more before it. He did not kill Voss. He loved him. Voss had finally found Vane's list and was going to deliver the file himself — and Hale killed him to stop it.

No single clue convicts Hale. The print alone could be a coffee run. The pharmacy record alone proves a favour. The file alone proves a motive, not a murder. Together, they leave no one else: only Hale knew the file was coming that night, only Hale had the medicine, and only Hale's print is on the lid.

subtitle: The Unit's founder is dead in his own archive. The sixth envelope is addressed to you.

suspects.alibi: Claims she was home alone from 21:00, preparing a brief. No witness. Her calendar says 'Voss — 21:30, archive,' and a car matching hers was seen near the Unit at 22:40.
lieList: The file does not exist. Harlan was an old man chasing ghosts.
suspects.motive: Voss was about to deliver the sealed 1998 file proving she buried exculpatory evidence — the end of her career, her reputation, and her freedom.
suspects.name: Corinne Hale
suspects.secret: In 1998, as defence attorney in the Harbor Lights trial, she buried a witness statement that would have freed her own client — because disclosing it would have exposed her firm's corruption. The man died in prison in 2009.
suspects.trustIntro: Composed, precise, furious at the accusation. She denies the file exists — until the print on its folder is shown to her.
truthList: I collected his refill because he asked me to. He was my father's oldest friend.
I brought him coffee that night.
I handled the sealed file. I knew what was in it.

suspects.alibi: Cataloguing in the archive basement from 21:00 to 23:00. The basement cameras have been broken for a year — no footage, but the catalog entries he made are timestamped through the night.
lieList: I do not know who sends the envelopes.
I have never been in Voss's office.
I was not in the archive that night.
suspects.motive: None against Voss — Voss was his partner, his friend, the only man who ever understood. His motive is the opposite: he spent twenty-eight years trying to undo what was buried.
suspects.name: Elias Vane
suspects.role: Cold Case Unit Archivist — THE ANCHORMAN
suspects.secret: He IS the Anchorman. For twenty-eight years he has sent black envelopes sealed with a silver anchor, nudging the Cold Case Unit to reopen the cases whose original files were compromised — six this season, twenty-two before it.
suspects.trustIntro: Quiet, precise, unafraid. He admits everything the moment the handwriting is matched — and asks only that you read the ledger.
truthList: Yes. I sent the envelopes. Every one of them.
I was cataloguing in the basement. The cameras there have been broken for a year.
In 1998, evidence was buried in the Harbor Lights trial. I found the copy. I could not prove who buried it.

suspects.alibi: At work until 23:00, verified by three colleagues and her office keycard. She never went near the Unit that night.
lieList: My father and I were close.
I never fought with him about the Unit.
suspects.motive: Inheritance — but Voss had already relented and changed the will back, and she never knew he had cut her out in the first place.
suspects.name: Mara Voss
suspects.secret: She and her father fought bitterly the week before he died — she told him the Unit was eating him alive — and he cut her out of his will the next day. He changed it back before he died; she never knew.
suspects.trustIntro: Grief first, anger second. She fought with him, and she will not pretend otherwise. But she was at work all night.
truthList: We fought. I told him the Unit was eating him alive.
He cut me out of his will. I did not know he changed it back.
I was at work until eleven. Ask my colleagues.

suspects.alibi: At the shelter all night, seen by twenty people, logged in at 20:00 and out at 07:00. He never left the building.
lieList: I have not spoken to him in years.
suspects.motive: Voss was going to name him in new testimony — but Jo's fear was of exposure, and he was twenty miles away, witnessed, all night.
suspects.name: Jo 'Fingers' Malone
suspects.secret: He was Voss's informant for twenty years, and Voss was about to name him in new testimony about the Harbor Lights trial. He begged Voss not to.
suspects.trustIntro: Frightened, then relieved when the shelter log is read. His note was a plea, not a threat.
truthList: Harlan was going to name me in new testimony. I begged him not to.
I was at the shelter all night. Twenty people saw me.
I have never been in that archive room.

suspects.alibi: Her 20:40 call to Voss went unanswered (call log confirms); she was at her flat from 21:00, on a video call with a friend until 23:00.
lieList: I have never leaked a file.
Voss and I had no problems.
suspects.motive: Voss was about to suspend her for leaking a file — a career blow, not a reason to kill the man who recruited her.
suspects.name: Det. Ana Reyes
suspects.secret: She leaked a closed-case file to a journalist, and Voss found out. He was going to suspend her the next morning.
suspects.trustIntro: Young, defensive, then honest. She leaked the file. She did not kill her captain.
truthList: I leaked a file to a journalist, yes. A closed case, nothing live.
Voss found out and was furious. He was going to suspend me.
I called him at 20:40. He did not answer.

title: The Anchorman

twists.body: Elias Vane admits it freely: he IS the Anchorman. He sent every envelope, for twenty-eight years. And his alibi for the murder is the weakest in the room — the basement cameras have been broken for a year. Is the man who pointed the Unit at the truth also the man who killed the one person who found him out?
twists.title: The archivist confesses

twists.body: The sealed file is recovered from the courthouse vault — and it names the person who buried the witness statement in 1998: not Vane, not Voss, but the defence attorney herself, Corinne Hale. The Anchorman was never the villain. He was the only person in the building who spent twenty-eight years trying to undo a crime the law had already forgiven. And Voss died because he finally agreed with him.
twists.title: The file names the burier
